one_line_contribution: Partition an agent's memory-free failures at a fixed sample budget into coverage failures (gold never generated) and selection failures (gold generated but outvoted), argue that injected experience can only repair the former while instruction optimization repairs the latter, and adjudicate memory's residual value with an agreement-gated-memory vs. agreement-gated-extra-sampling control at matched tokens (P4) plus a stratum-decomposed disjointness test between GEPA-style instructions and a self-editing bank (P6).
closest_prior_work: The coverage/selection split is not new; it is the pass@k-vs-maj@k (coverage vs. precision) decomposition of Brown et al., 'Large Language Monkeys' (arXiv:2407.21787), and the argument that a mechanism which only reweights already-sampled candidates cannot manufacture new ones is the central claim of the RLVR pass@k line (e.g. Yue et al., arXiv:2504.13837, 'Does RLVR Incentivize Reasoning Capacity Beyond the Base Model?'), which reaches it for RL post-training exactly as this proposal reaches it for instruction edits. Neither is cited anywhere in Related Work or the collision check. What genuinely survives is narrower than the proposal states: transplanting that known decomposition onto the memory-vs-prompt-optimizer question and running the AGS control. On the memory side, Evo-Memory (2511.20857) and arXiv:2511.04234 already report the likely headline (a trivial or memory-free baseline beats elaborate experience reuse at matched compute), and Difficulty-Adaptive SC already conditions low-agreement items on retrieved solved exemplars — which the proposal concedes and now runs as E3-ii, i.e. its nearest neighbour is inside its own baseline table.
strongest_objection: COVERAGE-FAIL is operationalized as 'gold absent from 8 samples of pool A', which makes it a property of the budget, not of the item — and the AGS arm in E3/P4 spends its extra tokens on precisely the low-agreement items whose gold answer has small but nonzero sampling probability. So the theory's load-bearing asymmetry ('sampling can only convert selection failures; only injected experience converts coverage failures') is false as implemented, and P4's mechanism attribution ('AGM's advantage concentrated in COVERAGE-FAIL') is confounded with the fact that AGS attacks the same stratum. This compounds with a power problem the Measurement section never addresses: the MDE analysis powers accuracy contrasts (3.1 points ≈ 25 net discordant items), but every mechanism prediction is a composition statistic over memory's fix set — and the proposal's own pilot says the bank fixed ZERO items and P1/P7 predict always-on memory loses. If MEM yields ~10 fixes, P2's '≥60% of fixes in COVERAGE-FAIL' has a confidence interval spanning most of the unit interval, and P6's 'Jaccard overlap < 0.25' is satisfied degenerately by an empty fix set rather than by any division of labour. P6 also asserts additivity 'within 1.5 points', a precision finer than the study's own 3.1-point MDE, so it cannot be established at n=800 in either direction. The paper's two declared legs (P2 mechanism, P6 coupling) are therefore unpowered as specified, leaving a bounded null on one Wikipedia multi-hop task with one 7B model — a result Evo-Memory and 2511.04234 substantially already report.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Report the coverage curve from pool A — fraction of items where gold first appears at n = 1,2,4,8,16,24 — and redefine COVERAGE-FAIL asymptotically (absent from all 24) with an explicit measured conversion rate of extra sampling inside that stratum; the recoverable-coverage ceiling then has to be stated net of what AGS itself recovers, otherwise E0's go/no-go number is inflated. (2) Add a power analysis for the stratum-composition statistics, and pre-register a minimum fix-count precondition (e.g. ≥40 MEM fixes and ≥40 INSTR fixes) below which P2/P6/P7 are reported as descriptive rather than as confirmatory tests; note explicitly that Jaccard is undefined when a fix set is near-empty and pre-specify the fallback. (3) Restate P6 as an equivalence test with a bound at or above the MDE, or reallocate items from the free pool reads to enlarge the E7 held-out set. (4) Run the coverage-targeted memory-free control described below, so P4 is against the strongest cheap coverage mechanism rather than against more T=0.7 samples. (5) Stop describing HotpotQA-distractor + HoVer as breadth — both are Wikipedia multi-hop EM tasks — and either add a genuinely different family or scope every claim to answer-aggregation Wikipedia QA in the title. (6) Cite and position against the pass@k coverage/precision line; it is the proposal's actual intellectual antecedent.
missing_baseline: Two. First and decisive: a coverage-targeted memory-free gated arm — same τ and n0, matched tokens, but the extra samples drawn at higher temperature and/or under prompt perturbation / diverse decoding (the proposal cuts the temperature sweep, and it cites arXiv:2608.09351 showing input-side diversity Pareto-dominates plain SC at matched cost). AGS as specified redraws at the identical T=0.7 from the identical prompt, which is the weakest possible coverage mechanism; if AGM beats that AGS but loses to a high-temperature or perturbed AGS, P4 collapses and the paper's decisive contrast was rigged toward memory. Second: memory-as-reranker — retrieved experience used only to select among pool-A candidates at answer time, never placed in the generation prefix. It is nearly free from existing pools, has zero SOLVED-HIGH breakage by construction, and is the obvious engineering response to the paper's own mechanism (memory helps coverage, hurts selection); a reviewer will ask why the proposal tests only prefix injection and then generalizes to 'agent memory'.
preprint_collision: Weak, and the proposal says so itself: this round's search returned nothing because the tool hit a hard usage limit, so the positioning is explicitly carried over and unverified. Per the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this costs the submission — the commitment to 'run a structured search before submission' is not evidence available at review time. Beyond the tool failure, the check is thin in the exact place novelty is claimed: its query list ('coverage vs selection failure sampling') never surfaces the pass@k coverage/precision literature (Large Language Monkeys 2407.21787; the RLVR-pass@k line, e.g. 2504.13837; verification-bottleneck work on sample-scrutinize-scale), which is where the surviving conceptual contribution actually originates. I cannot name a preprint that runs the exact AGM-vs-AGS control with a stratum decomposition over agent memory, so the specific control looks unclaimed; but the two conceded collisions (MemRL 2601.03192, MemDelta 2606.29914) plus Evo-Memory 2511.20857 and 2511.04234 already occupy the compute-matched-memory-loses conclusion, which is the outcome the proposal's own pilot and P1/P7 predict it will reach.
